title: Vodka sauce with tomatoes and cream

content.title: About
content.content: Vodka sauce with tomatoes and cream is a classic Italian-inspired sauce where a tomato base is combined with the aromatic kick of vodka and the richness of cream. It is commonly served over pasta, especially penne or fettuccine. The vodka helps release the flavor of the tomatoes, while the cream gives the sauce a silky, smooth texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The “Vodka” sauce originated in the United States in the 1980s, though its roots trace back to Italian cuisine.
Vodka is used not for its alcohol content but to emulsify fats and enhance tomato flavor.
Traditional recipes call for only one to two tablespoons of vodka, but the amount can be adjusted to taste.
Cream used is usually 10‑30 % fat; higher‑fat cream yields a thicker sauce.
The sauce keeps well in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, but is best served freshly made.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and skin.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes contain vitamin C, which helps boost the immune system.

items.title: Contains calcium and vitamin D from cream
items.content: Cream adds calcium and a modest amount of vitamin D, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Moderate healthy fats
items.content: The cream contributes saturated and monounsaturated fats that can fit into a balanced diet.

items.title: Improves nutrient absorption
items.content: The small amount of alcohol enhances the bioavailability of certain tomato antioxidants.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Although most alcohol evaporates during cooking, trace amounts may remain, which should be considered by those avoiding alcohol.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Cream and oil make the sauce calorie‑rich; portion control is advisable for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream contains lactose, so lactose‑intolerant individuals may opt for dairy‑free alternatives.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Tomato paste and pre‑made sauces can be salty; taste and adjust salt as needed.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the sauce hot over pasta, rice, or vegetable dishes. It can be stirred into casseroles, used as a pizza base, or served as a dip with bread. For extra brightness, finish with fresh basil or grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the sauce to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat gently on low heat, adding a splash of cream or water to restore its creamy consistency.
